title: Journal v2: schema-validated, indexed run journals
summary: The checkpoint runner's journal grows from a two-payload buffer into a versioned, schema-validated event log. Events now carry a typed actor (harness, person, or the engine's own `system`), an optional work item and change, and a cost; eight payload types replace two. Every append is validated against a draft 2020-12 JSON schema before a byte is written, a run-complete event must name the current chain head and closes the run, and the first accepted event records the run in a per-work-item index guarded by a lock file. The buffer directory is renamed to `runs`, and a new reader replays a journal link by link, refusing a broken chain rather than returning a partial list.

nodes.label: Checkpoint runner
nodes.subtitle: osf verify --checkpoint
nodes.summary: Runs the checkpoint's moon tasks and writes one verification event per task plus a checkpoint-complete event. Now builds its actor with `Actor::system("osf")` and fills the new `check_type`, `summary` and typed `EvidenceGrade` fields.

nodes.label: Post-tool hook
nodes.subtitle: osf hook post-tool
nodes.summary: Writes verification events for a single tool invocation. Unchanged in behaviour; its tests now read the `runs` directory instead of `buffer`.

nodes.label: Journal writer
nodes.subtitle: Journal::append_draft
nodes.summary: Computes the chain hash, serialises the event, validates it against the schema, checks a run-complete event's head hash, records the run in the work-item index on the first accepted event, then appends one JSON line. A refused event writes nothing and leaves the head unchanged; no event is accepted after run-complete.

nodes.label: Event model
nodes.subtitle: Event, Actor, Payload, Cost
nodes.summary: The versioned envelope and its eight payload types: run-started, verification, review, finding, state-change, run-complete, attention, checkpoint-complete. Adds the `system` actor kind, `Change`, `Cost`, `EvidenceGrade`, `Severity`, `WorkItemState` and `BlockedCause`.

nodes.label: Hash chain
nodes.subtitle: event_hash / HashInput
nodes.summary: SHA-256 over the previous hash, a newline, and the canonical JSON of payload, work item, change, actor and cost. `run`, `timestamp_ms` and `schema_version` stay outside the digest; `duration_ms` and `cache` are now inside it, so a rerun with different timings hashes differently.

nodes.label: Journal reader
nodes.subtitle: read_run
nodes.summary: Replays a run's journal, checking each line's schema, run id, prev_hash and recomputed hash in order. Any failure returns that line's error and no events, so a caller never sees a partial chain; `complete` reports whether the last event was run-complete.

nodes.label: Run index
nodes.subtitle: record_run / runs_for_work_item
nodes.summary: One JSON file per work item under `<state_dir>/index`, named by the SHA-256 hex of the work item id, listing that item's run ids in recorded order. Writes go through a temporary file renamed over the target, serialised by a lock file that is reclaimed after 60 seconds of staleness.

nodes.label: Schema validator
nodes.subtitle: schema::validate
nodes.summary: Compiles the event schema once per process and checks each serialised event against it, returning one reason per problem with its JSON path. The writer calls it before every append; the reader calls it on every line.

nodes.label: Event schema
nodes.subtitle: draft 2020-12
nodes.summary: The JSON Schema for one event envelope: required fields, the eight event types, per-type payload shapes, and the conditional rules — a harness actor must name a model, a blocked state change must carry a cause, a non-observed finding must not name a verifier, and a work item must be provider-qualified.

nodes.label: runs/
nodes.subtitle: <run>.jsonl
nodes.summary: The per-run journal files, renamed from `buffer/`. Each run is its own hash chain starting from genesis; opening a run id whose file already holds events is refused.

nodes.label: index/
nodes.subtitle: <sha256>.json + .lock
nodes.summary: Per-work-item run lists, plus the lock files that serialise writers. A malformed index or one naming another work item is refused, never silently replaced.

nodes.label: CI checkpoint evidence
nodes.subtitle: upload-artifact
nodes.summary: The CI job that uploads checkpoint evidence now collects `$OSF_STATE_DIR/runs` instead of `$OSF_STATE_DIR/buffer`.

edges.label: append(actor, payload)
edges.summary: The checkpoint runner hands each verification and the checkpoint-complete event to the writer, which validates and chains it.
The post-tool hook writes its verification events through the same writer.

edges.label: validate(event)
edges.summary: Every append validates the serialised event before any byte reaches the file.

edges.label: include_str!
edges.summary: The schema is embedded in the binary and compiled once per process.

edges.label: event_hash(HashInput)
edges.summary: The writer computes the next link from the previous hash and the event's hashed parts.

edges.label: record_run
edges.summary: The first accepted event of a run records the run in its work item's index before the journal line is written; a failed index update refuses the event.

edges.label: one JSON line
edges.summary: The event is appended as one JSON line with a trailing newline.

edges.label: temp file + rename
edges.summary: The index is written through a temporary sibling renamed over the target, so a reader never sees a half-written list.
The reader loads a run's journal file and checks every line and link in order.
Each line is validated against the schema before it is deserialised into an event.

edges.label: recompute
edges.summary: The reader recomputes each event's hash and compares it with the stored one, reporting a mismatch as a broken chain at that line.
Both live in the journal module and share the run-id validation and SHA-256 helper.

edges.label: artifact path
edges.summary: CI now uploads the `runs` directory as checkpoint evidence.

flows.title: Appending one journal event
flows.summary: What happens between a caller handing over a payload and a validated, chained line landing in the run's journal file.

messages.label: append(actor, payload)
messages.note: The caller supplies an actor, a timestamp and a payload; the journal fills in the run, work item, change, prev_hash and hash.

messages.label: run already complete?
messages.note: Once a run-complete event is accepted, every later append is refused before anything else happens.

messages.label: event_hash(HashInput)
messages.note: SHA-256 over prev_hash, a newline, and the canonical JSON of payload, work item, change, actor and cost.

messages.label: validate(event)
messages.note: The serialised event is checked against the embedded schema; each problem comes back with its JSON path.

messages.label: run-complete head_hash == head?
messages.note: A run-complete event must name the journal's current head hash, so a run cannot close over a chain it did not see.

messages.label: record_run(work_item, run)
messages.note: Only on the first accepted event of a run, and only when the journal carries a work item. A failure here refuses the event before any line is written.

messages.label: lock, read, append, rename
messages.note: The index is read under a lock file, the run appended if absent, and the result written through a temporary file renamed over the target.

messages.label: one JSON line
messages.note: The validated event is appended to `<state_dir>/runs/<run>.jsonl` and the chain head advances.

flows.title: Replaying a run's journal
flows.summary: How a reader reconstructs a run's chain and what it refuses along the way.

messages.label: read <run>.jsonl
messages.note: A missing file is NotFound; an unsafe run id is refused before any path is built.

messages.label: validate(line)
messages.note: Each line is checked against the schema before it is deserialised, so a schema-invalid line is reported as invalid even when its hash is correct.

messages.label: recompute hash
messages.note: The reader recomputes the event's hash from its own fields and compares it with the stored one.

messages.label: prev_hash == head?
messages.note: A mismatch, a deleted line, a swapped pair or an event from another run all surface as ChainBroken at the offending line.

messages.label: events, head_hash, complete
messages.note: Any failure returns that line's error and no events at all, so a caller never sees a partial chain.
